RedKinNet: selection of unrelated individuals from kinship networks

Source: R/RedKinNet-package.R
RedKinNet-package.Rd

Genetic studies often need a set of individuals with no close relatives among them. RedKinNet joins every pair of related individuals in a network and selects a maximum set of unrelated individuals: a set with no related pair of the largest possible size (see rkn_selection). The families, the connected components of the network, are resolved by structural rules and by an exact search that also handles the large and intricate families of genetic isolates.

A typical analysis follows these steps:

  1. rkn_check_samples flags possible duplicates and contaminated samples in the kinship estimates;

  2. rkn_graph_from_kinship builds the network at a kinship threshold, optionally leaving samples out and adding covariates;

  3. a selector chooses the individuals: rkn_select_random at random, optionally uniformly among all the maximum sets with exact inclusion probabilities; rkn_select_criteria by preferences for individuals, such as women; or rkn_select_global towards a target composition of the whole selection, such as half women or a mean age, after rkn_tradeoff has shown what the target costs in selection size;

  4. the returned rkn_selection object is inspected with print(), summary() and plot() (see rkn_plot_pre).
